title: Equivariant discrete coefficient equivalences preserve continuous cohomology across universes
statement:
Let $G$ be a topological group in universe $u$. Let $M,N$ be integer modules,
with discrete topologies and actions of $G$ by linear automorphisms, in universes
$\max(u,s)$ and $\max(u,t)$ respectively. Let $e:M\simeq_{\mathbf Z}N$ be a linear
equivalence with $e(gx)=g e(x)$ for every $g\in G$ and $x\in M$.
For every $q\in\mathbf N$ there is a type equivalence
$H^q_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,M)\simeq H^q_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,N)$.
The continuous cohomology here is homology in topological integer modules of the
homogeneous cochain complex: degree $n$ is the invariant submodule of $n+1$ iterated
continuous-map spaces, where the action on a map is $(g f)(x)=g(f(g^{-1}x))$.
Starting with constant insertion from coefficients to continuous maps, its differential
is recursively constant insertion minus the previous differential applied pointwise.
Joint continuity of the group action is not required.

proof.text: Make e a continuous representation equivalence: discrete topologies give continuity in both directions, and integer scalar multiplication agrees with integer repeated addition even when the bundled module instances differ. Recursively postcompose through coinduction to obtain equivalences of every resolution term. Restrict their equivariant maps to invariants. The recursive differential commutes with these maps by induction, using preservation of subtraction; off-shape differentials are zero. This is implemented by coindEquiv, resolutionEquiv, resolutionEquiv_d, invariantsEquiv, cochainsEquiv and cochainsEquiv_d.

For the short complexes at degree q, restrict the middle linear equivalence to the kernels, using the commuting outgoing map and injectivity of the next equivalence. The commuting incoming map and surjectivity of the preceding equivalence identify the boundary ranges. Apply Submodule.Quotient.equiv to obtain inverse equivalences of kernel modulo image, including across universes. TopModuleCat.isLimitKer and isColimitCoker give concrete left homology data; their homologyIso identifies the categorical homology with these quotients. Compose the underlying equivalences. This is implemented by concreteData and shortComplexEquiv, entirely in Mathlib.
